scenes.purpose: Introduce the main topic of elections in India.
scenes.teacher_script: Today, we will explore the process of elections in India, a fundamental aspect of our democratic system. We'll learn how representatives are chosen to govern our states.

scenes.purpose: Explain the role of the Election Commission and the frequency of elections.
scenes.teacher_script: The Election Commission of India is responsible for conducting fair elections for all state assemblies. These elections are typically held once every five years.

scenes.purpose: Describe who can vote and the concept of constituencies.
scenes.teacher_script: Citizens must register as voters in their local constituency to participate. All voters in one constituency elect a single member to the Assembly.

scenes.purpose: Detail the eligibility criteria for candidates and types of candidates.
scenes.teacher_script: To contest elections, a person must be an Indian citizen and at least twenty-five years old. Candidates can represent political parties or stand as 'Independents'.

bullets: Do not belong to any party

scenes.purpose: Explain the system of reservation in constituencies.
scenes.teacher_script: To ensure adequate representation for weaker sections, the Indian Constitution reserves certain constituencies. These are specifically for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
